question: The concepts no double jeopardy, no self incrimination and no ex post facto are mentioned under _____ of the Indian Constitution. (RRB JE CBT-I 2024 (17/12/2024) Shift 1)
options: Article 20
Article 21
Article 19
Article 23
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Article 20

Explanation:
Article 20 of the Indian Constitution provides protection against conviction in certain cases. It includes three key safeguards: no ex post facto law, no double jeopardy, and no self-incrimination. This article protects individuals from being punished for an act that was not an offense at the time it was committed. It ensures that no person is prosecuted and punished for the same offense more than once, and that no person accused of any offense shall be compelled to be a witness against themselves. Article 21 deals with the right to life and personal liberty, Article 19 with freedom of speech, and Article 23 with the prohibition of human trafficking.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ No double jeopardy → Under Article 20(2)
☛ Right against self-incrimination → Enshrined in Article 20(3)
☛ Prohibition of ex post facto law → Article 20(1)
☛ Article 20 is a Fundamental Right → Part of Part III
☛ Article 20 applies only in criminal cases → Not civil cases
question_hi: भारतीय संविधान के _____ में दोषसिद्धि के मामले में कुछ अधिकारों के संरक्षण से संबंधित अवधारणाएँ जैसे दोहरा खतरा नहीं, स्वयं को दोषी नहीं ठहराना और पूर्वव्यापी कानून नहीं, का उल्लेख किया गया है। (RRB JE CBT-I 2024 (17/12/2024) Shift 1)
options_hi: अनुच्छेद 20
अनुच्छेद 21
अनुच्छेद 19
अनुच्छेद 23
solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है अनुच्छेद 20

Explanation:
भारतीय संविधान का अनुच्छेद 20 दोषसिद्धि के मामले में कुछ अधिकारों का संरक्षण प्रदान करता है। इसमें तीन प्रमुख सुरक्षाएँ शामिल हैं: पूर्वव्यापी कानून नहीं (Ex post facto law), दोहरा खतरा नहीं (Double jeopardy), और स्वयं को दोषी नहीं ठहराना (Self-incrimination)। यह अनुच्छेद किसी व्यक्ति को ऐसे अपराध के लिए दंडित होने से बचाता है जो घटित होने के समय कानून का उल्लंघन नहीं था। यह सुनिश्चित करता है कि किसी व्यक्ति को एक ही अपराध के लिए एक से अधिक बार दंडित न किया जाए और कोई भी व्यक्ति अपने विरुद्ध गवाही देने के लिए बाध्य न हो। अनुच्छेद 21 जीवन और व्यक्तिगत स्वतंत्रता से, अनुच्छेद 19 अभिव्यक्ति की स्वतंत्रता से, और अनुच्छेद 23 मानव तस्करी के निषेध से संबंधित है।

question: How many members of the Rajya Sabha are nominated by the President of India? (RRB JE CBT-I 2024 (17/12/2024) Shift 2)
options: 15
8
10
12
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 12

Explanation:
According to Article 80 of the Indian Constitution, the maximum strength of the Rajya Sabha is 250 members. Out of these, 238 members are elected by the legislative assemblies of states and union territories, while 12 members are nominated by the President of India. These nominated members are individuals having special knowledge or practical experience in fields such as literature, art, science, and social service. The President nominates them to ensure expertise and diversity in the House. This provision falls under Part V of the Constitution. The term of nominated members is 6 years, same as other Rajya Sabha members. The Rajya Sabha is the upper house of Parliament and represents the states of India.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:

☛ Which article describes the composition of Rajya Sabha? → Article 80
☛ What is the term of nominated members of Rajya Sabha? → 6 years
☛ From which fields are nominated members chosen? → Literature, art, science, social service
☛ How many Rajya Sabha members are elected by states? → 238

question: Which of the following disputes is excluded from the original jurisdiction of the Supreme Court? (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (21/06/2025) Shift 3)
options: A commercial contract dispute between Gujarat and a private company
A disagreement between Punjab and Haryana over territorial boundaries
A dispute between Maharashtra and the Centre over a constitutional law issue
A dispute between Karnataka and Tamil Nadu over water sharing
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is A dispute between Karnataka and Tamil Nadu over water sharing

Explanation:
Under Article 131 of the Indian Constitution, the original jurisdiction of the Supreme Court extends only to disputes between states and the Centre, or between states inter se, involving legal or factual questions. However, inter-state water disputes are governed by the Inter-State Water Disputes Act, 1956, which provides for the constitution of a Water Disputes Tribunal for adjudication, thereby excluding them from the Supreme Court's original jurisdiction. Thus, the Cauvery water dispute between Karnataka and Tamil Nadu is excluded. The other options—constitutional disputes between a state and Centre, boundary disputes between states—fall within original jurisdiction. Disputes with private parties are also excluded, but the correct answer is the water dispute.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ Article 131 → Original jurisdiction of the Supreme Court
☛ Inter-State Water Disputes Act, 1956 → Tribunal for water disputes
☛ Article 262 → Parliament may provide for adjudication of inter-state water disputes
☛ Cauvery water dispute → Between Karnataka and Tamil Nadu
☛ Original jurisdiction covers → Legal disputes between states or state vs Centre
question_hi: निम्नलिखित में से कौन सा विवाद उच्चतम न्यायालय के मूल अधिकार क्षेत्र से बाहर है? (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (21/06/2025) Shift 3)

प्रादेशिक सीमाओं को लेकर पंजाब और हरियाणा के बीच असहमति
संवैधानिक कानून के मुद्दे पर महाराष्ट्र और केंद्र के बीच विवाद

Explanation:
भारतीय संविधान के अनुच्छेद 131 के तहत उच्चतम न्यायालय के मूल अधिकार क्षेत्र में केवल राज्यों और केंद्र के बीच या राज्यों आपस में उत्पन्न विवाद शामिल हैं, जिनमें कानूनी या तथ्यात्मक प्रश्न शामिल हों। लेकिन जल विवाद अधिनियम 1956 के तहत अंतर-राज्यीय जल विवादों का निपटारा जल विवाद न्यायाधिकरण द्वारा किया जाता है, न कि सीधे सर्वोच्च न्यायालय में। अतः कर्नाटक और तमिलनाडु के बीच कावेरी जल बंटवारे का विवाद सर्वोच्च न्यायालय के मूल क्षेत्राधिकार से बाहर है। अन्य विकल्पों में, राज्य और केंद्र या दो राज्यों के बीच संवैधानिक या प्रादेशिक विवाद न्यायालय के मूल क्षेत्राधिकार में आते हैं। निजी कंपनी से विवाद भी मूल क्षेत्राधिकार में नहीं आता, परंतु यह विकल्प सही नहीं है।

question: Who among the following first coined the term 'judicial activism'? (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (19/06/2025) Shift 1)
options: DA Desai
Arthur Schlesinger Jr.
Justice PN Bhagwati
Justice VR Krishna Iyer
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Arthur Schlesinger Jr.

Explanation:
The term 'judicial activism' was first coined by Arthur Schlesinger Jr. in 1947 in an article published in Fortune Magazine. It refers to the propensity of the judiciary to actively interpret the Constitution, particularly when the legislature or executive fails to perform its duties. In India, Justice P.N. Bhagwati and Justice V.R. Krishna Iyer are considered proponents of judicial activism, but they did not coin the term. D.A. Desai was an Indian judge but not directly associated with coining the term. Judicial activism emerged as a key concept in U.S. constitutional law before spreading to other jurisdictions.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ Who coined the term 'judicial activism'? → Arthur Schlesinger Jr.
☛ Where and when was it first used? → Fortune Magazine, 1947
☛ Who are regarded as pioneers of judicial activism in India? → Justice P.N. Bhagwati and Justice V.R. Krishna Iyer
☛ Landmark case associated with judicial activism in India → Kesavananda Bharati case (basic structure doctrine)
☛ What is the opposite of judicial activism? → Judicial restraint

question: Who elects the members of the Estimates Committee in the Indian Parliament?  (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (24/06/2025) Shift 3)
options: Members of the Lok Sabha
Prime Minister
Members of the Rajya Sabha
President of India
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Members of the Lok Sabha

Explanation:
The Estimates Committee of the Indian Parliament is a key financial committee that examines government expenditures. Its members are elected by the Members of the Lok Sabha, not by the Prime Minister, Rajya Sabha, or President. The committee consists of 30 members, elected annually by Lok Sabha members through the principle of proportional representation. This committee ensures financial discipline by scrutinizing estimates and reporting back to Parliament.

question: Which Indian Constitution Act provides for the minimization of inequalities in income, property, facilities and opportunities in the Directive Principles of State Policy? (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (24/06/2025) Shift 3)
options: 42nd Constitutional Amendment 1976
97th Constitutional Amendment 2011
86th Constitutional Amendment 2002
44th Constitutional Amendment 1978
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 44th Constitutional Amendment 1978

Explanation:
The 44th Constitutional Amendment (1978) added Article 38(2) to the Directive Principles of State Policy, which directs the State to minimize inequalities in income, property, facilities and opportunities. This amendment was brought by the Morarji Desai government to restore democratic values after the Emergency. It specifically mandates that the State shall strive to reduce inequalities in status, facilities and opportunities, not only among individuals but also among groups residing in different areas or engaged in different vocations. Thus, the 44th Amendment is the correct answer as it directly inserts the provision regarding minimization of inequalities in the Directive Principles.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ Which article was amended by the 44th Amendment regarding inequalities? → Article 38
☛ In which year was the 44th Constitutional Amendment passed? → 1978
☛ Who was the Prime Minister during the 44th Amendment? → Morarji Desai
☛ What is the main objective of Article 38(2)? → Reduce income and property inequalities
☛ Where are Directive Principles located in the Constitution? → Part IV (Articles 36-51)

question: Which of the following policy adoptions by the Government of India is NOT guided by the 'Directive Principles of State Policy? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (27/02/2021) Shift 2)
options: Promotion of village panchayats
Preparation of building by-laws
Uniform civil code
Prohibition of consumption of alcoholic liquor
solution:

Explanation:
The Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP) in Part IV of the Indian Constitution guide the government in policy-making. Article 40 relates to the promotion of village panchayats. The Supreme Court has given a wide interpretation to this article, including the right to live with dignity, right to a clean environment, right to privacy, and right to a speedy trial. question: The 100th Amendment (2015) to the constitution of India is related to: (RRB NTPC CBT-I (23/07/2021) Shift 2)
options: a maximum of 10% reservation for the economically weaker sections
establishment of the National Judicial Appointment Commission
ratification of the land boundary agreement between India and Bangladesh
introduction of the Goods and Services Tax
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is ratification of the land boundary agreement between India and Bangladesh

Explanation:
The 100th Amendment Act of 2015 to the Indian Constitution is related to the ratification of the Land Boundary Agreement (LBA) between India and Bangladesh. This amendment modified the First Schedule of the Constitution to enable the exchange of enclaves along the India-Bangladesh border. Under this agreement, India transferred approximately 111 enclaves to Bangladesh, while Bangladesh transferred 51 enclaves to India. The LBA resolved long-standing border disputes and provided rights to residents of these enclaves. The amendment was passed under Article 2 and Article 3 of the Constitution, which allow for the admission or establishment of new states and alteration of boundaries. The 100th Amendment is historic as it finalized the land boundary between the two nations.

question: Which article empowers the Indian parliament to include in or exclude caste, race, tribes from the list of Schedule castes? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (08/04/2021) Shift 2)

question: Who chairs the joint sitting of the two houses of the Parliament? (RPF SI 2018 (13/01/2019) Shift 2)
options: Prime Minister
President
Speaker of Lok Sabha
Chairman of Rajya Sabha
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Speaker of Lok Sabha

Explanation:
According to Article 108 of the Indian Constitution, the joint sitting of both houses of Parliament is chaired by the Speaker of the Lok Sabha. In the absence of the Speaker, the Deputy Speaker of the Lok Sabha presides. A joint sitting is called when a bill passed by one house is rejected by the other or remains pending for more than six months. So far, three joint sittings have been held: the Dowry Prohibition Bill (1961), the Banking Service Commission Bill (1977), and the Prevention of Terrorism Bill (2002). The President can summon the joint sitting but does not preside over it.

question: Which British Prime Minister sent the Cripps Mission to India? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (04/02/2021) Shift 2)
options: Robert Walpole
Benjamin Disraeli
Margaret Thatcher
Winston Churchill
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Winston Churchill

Explanation:
The Cripps Mission was sent to India in 1942 by the British Prime Minister Winston Churchill. It was led by Sir Stafford Cripps. The mission aimed to negotiate with Indian leaders for Indian cooperation during World War II. It proposed granting India Dominion status after the war. The Congress wanted immediate independence, while the Muslim League did not receive clear assurance regarding the demand for Pakistan. After the failure of the Cripps Mission, the Quit India Movement was launched.

भारत में ब्रिटिश शासन का अंत 15 अगस्त 1947 को हुआ, जब भारतीय स्वतंत्रता अधिनियम 1947 लागू हुआ। इस अधिनियम ने ब्रिटिश भारत को दो स्वतंत्र राष्ट्रों, भारत और पाकिस्तान में विभाजित किया। यह तारीख भारत की आजादी के रूप में मनाई जाती है। लॉर्ड माउंटबेटन ने अंतिम वायसराय के रूप में कार्य किया और स्वतंत्रता के बाद भारत के पहले गवर्नर-जनरल बने। जवाहरलाल नेहरू स्वतंत्र भारत के पहले प्रधानमंत्री बने। यह घटना ब्रिटिश साम्राज्य के पतन और एशिया में उपनिवेशवाद के अंत का प्रतीक है।
